shown.claim: 93% of Costa Rican tech companies save time on repetitive tasks with AI.
shown.source: PROCOMER 2025 Caracterización del Sector TIC, via El Financiero
shown.note: data.md figure matches exactly (93%). Reported via El Financiero's coverage of the Procomer study, not a direct Procomer publication link; CR scope.

shown.claim: Only 9% have a formal AI policy.
shown.source: PROCOMER 2025 Caracterización del Sector TIC's Costa Rica
shown.note: 9% have formal AI governance policies (data.md also notes 12% have dedicated AI/ML teams, not used here). CR-specific; adoption (76%) far outpaces governance.

shown.claim: 47% of employees have ever received any AI training.
shown.source: KPMG x Melbourne Business School, Trust, attitudes and use of AI: A global study 2025
shown.note: 47% received AI training (data.md also notes 40% have a workplace gen-AI policy, not used here). Global, 48,000+ people across 47 countries, fieldwork Nov 2024-Jan 2025.

shown.claim: Beginners who are taught get up to 34% more done.
shown.source: Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond, NBER Working Paper 31161, Generative AI at Work
shown.note: +34% productivity gain for novice/low-skilled customer-support agents using an AI assistant (vs ~0% for experts, +14% avg overall). Global/US; single Fortune 500 software firm, 5,179 agents.

alsoRead.claim: CR tech/TIC companies already use generative AI tools or digital agents in operations
alsoRead.source: PROCOMER, Caracterización del Sector TIC's Costa Rica 2025 (86 companies)
alsoRead.note: Headline CR adoption stat; small sample (86 companies) but a real local dataset.

alsoRead.claim: CR TIC firms cut product development cycle time with AI
alsoRead.figure: 70% reduction in dev cycles; 3-5 day reduction per functionality
alsoRead.note: Concrete CR efficiency figure; 2026 article covering 2025 Procomer data.

alsoRead.claim: CR ranks as Latin America's leader in AI human-talent/skills
alsoRead.figure: #1 in region (5th overall in ILIA composite)
alsoRead.note: Regional differentiator to lead with; not an adoption/usage stat.

alsoRead.claim: CR jobs theoretically exposed to large-language-model automation
alsoRead.figure: 19.2% of total CR employment exposed (2023 analysis)
alsoRead.source: La Nación, citing MICITT/Anthropic/OpenAI GDPval/OECD/IDB/WEF/McKinsey analyses
alsoRead.note: Belief-vs-evidence material; 53% of exposed jobs are high-skilled, 0% low-skilled.

alsoRead.claim: Gap between AI's theoretical task coverage and its practical use in knowledge work
alsoRead.figure: AI could do 94% of knowledge-work tasks in theory, but is practically used for only 33%
alsoRead.source: La Nación, citing same CR analysis
alsoRead.note: Strong 'task not whole job' puzzle fact; CR/global.

alsoRead.claim: Organizations regularly using AI in at least one business function
alsoRead.source: McKinsey, The state of AI in 2025
alsoRead.note: Global adoption headline; contrast with McKinsey's own 5.5% real-ROI figure elsewhere in data.md.

alsoRead.claim: Most enterprise generative AI pilots fail to show P&L impact
alsoRead.figure: 95% of pilots deliver no measurable financial return; only 5% extract real value
alsoRead.source: MIT Project NANDA, The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025
alsoRead.note: Core failure-mode-3 stat; 52 exec interviews, 153 leader survey, 300 deployments. Global.

alsoRead.claim: Global belief that AI will shrink the job market
alsoRead.figure: 46% median across 37 countries say AI will mean fewer jobs; only 9% say more jobs

alsoRead.claim: Employees "bring their own AI" to work, bypassing company tools/oversight
alsoRead.figure: 78% of AI users use personal AI tools at work (BYOAI); 80% at SMBs

alsoRead.claim: Orgs report using AI in at least one function, per Stanford AI Index
alsoRead.source: Stanford HAI, 2025 AI Index Report, Economy chapter
alsoRead.note: Independent confirmation of McKinsey adoption trend; global.

alsoRead.claim: Knowledge workers using GPT-4 on "inside the frontier" tasks did more, faster, better work
alsoRead.source: Harvard Business School + BCG, Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier
alsoRead.note: Strong quality/speed uplift stat, paired with caveat elsewhere in data.md: -19% accuracy on tasks outside AI's competence. Global; 758 BCG consultants.
